name: FL-17
label: Likely R

key_factors: Incumbency advantage in a low-profile race
model.rationale: The R+10 district, Steube's overwhelming financial edge, and markets pricing him near 94% all point to a comfortable Republican hold, with no polls or ratings suggesting movement toward the underfunded Democratic challenger. The forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based baseline.
model.watch: Any late polling or outside spending targeting Steube could tighten the race, but there is currently no evidence of either.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Republican incumbent Greg Steube seeks another term in this southwest Florida district, which leans about ten points Republican. He enters the general election with roughly $2.1 million on hand after raising over $1.3 million, while Democratic challenger Matthew Montavon has raised under $100,000 and holds only about $24,000. An independent candidate trails far behind in both fundraising and profile.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and money. Prediction markets give Steube about a 94% chance of winning. The combination of the district's partisan lean, incumbency, and the lopsided financial picture points to a comfortable Republican win, though the absence of polling leaves some room for uncertainty.
